newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico key Cetes rate higher on market pressures.
newsitem.headline: Mexico key Cetes rate higher on market pressures.

text.p: Mexico's bellwether one-month Cetes rose at the Banco de Mexico primary auction on Tuesday, pushed higher by pressure in the secondary market, analysts said.
Mexican banks will have to square their books with the central bank tomorrow and that generally squeezes liquidity in the secondary market, they said.
That pressure in the secondary market was offset to some degree, however, by stability in the U.S. bond market, which helped moderate upward pressure on Mexican rates.
The yield on the 28-day Cetes rose 54 basis points to 18.91 percent, and rose 30 basis points on 91-day paper to 20.79 percent at the primary auction.
The 182-day paper was flat at 21.85 percent, while the yield on one-year paper fell nine basis points to 23.06 percent as the yield curve flattened out.
A survey of nine dealers earlier in the day by Reuters found expectations of an increase of 76 basis points on the one-month paper, and smaller increases further out the yield curve.

"The increase in rates in the short-term simply reflects demand for liquidity, but the stability in the long-term reflects the solid fundamentals that are reflected in the economy," said Santander Investment economist Enrique Ramirez.

He said rates in Mexico are near their floor and movements in the short-term will depend on what happens in the United States as markets await the next meeting of the Open Market Committee of the U.S. Federal Reserve.
The increase on the one-month paper comes after declines in the last three weeks, and analysts said the increase was expected.

"I think that it was a healthy movement since rates appeared to have fallen too far, and when rates fall too far there is a tendency for them to turn the other way very strongly and this is what we need to avoid -- everyone wants rates to fall, but smoothly," Mexico City economist Jonathan Heath said.
Demand fell slightly this week, to 12.99 billion pesos for the 3.0 billion on offer. Last week demand was 13.04 billion.
